newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-JAPAN, SOUTH KOREA MEET FIFA OVER 2002 WORLD CUP FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JAPAN, SOUTH KOREA MEET FIFA OVER 2002 WORLD CUP FINALS.

text.p: Japanese and Korean officials were meeting FIFA officials on Wednesday to begin dealing with the myriad of problems arising from the two countries co-hosting the 2002 World Cup finals.
A security blanket was placed around FIFA's headquarters with media representatives locked out until a news briefing later in the day.
One FIFA official said there was not enough room in the building for all the reporters and TV crews, many of whom had flown from Korea and Japan.
The meeting is the first official one since FIFA's general secretary Sepp Blatter expressed unease in a magazine article about the way the two countries had begun their joint venture.
Blatter was quoted as saying: "Japan and South Korea are not only not coming closer together, its quite the opposite. They are moving further apart. This is not the marriage we want."
Among the issues still be settled are who should host the final and how many teams should take part.
Delegates were meeting FIFA's 2002 Study Group members Guillermo Canedo of Mexico, Antonio Matarrese of Italy and Blatter.
On the eve of the meeting, South Korean officials seemed ahead in the public relations battle of appearing conciliatory.
While Japanese officials, have already staked out their positions on key points, the South Koreans say they are in Zurich respecting "the principle of equal opportunities".
Ken Naganuma, head of Japan's 2002 World Cup Committee, said last week: "It is imperative that FIFA come out with a course of action as soon as possible."
Japan, always lukewarm to the idea of co-hosting, already has forthrightly asked FIFA to give it the right to stage both the final and the opening match, informed sources said.
